site.title: Jalaranu
site.description: Explore the world's first underlake datacenter project: Jalaranu's validation approach and partnership opportunities for computing infrastructure in Indonesia.
site.footerTagline: Jalaranu - developing an underlake datacenter project to support Indonesia's digital resilience. The project evaluates thermal efficiency, operational reliability, and environmental effects through a staged, evidence-led program before any commitment to construction.

site.brandSlogan: Cold, silent, a sustainable data realm. The world's first underlake datacenter project.

about.seoDescription: Discover the story behind the world's first underlake datacenter project: Jalaranu's identity, development principles, and the people responsible.

hero.h1: Rooted in Indonesian identity. Developed through evidence.
hero.body: Jalaranu is developing an underlake datacenter and treats Indonesia's lakes as strategic national assets that must be understood before they are used. We turn that ambition into a **measurable process**: questions and methods are published up front, and findings are shared with their evidence and limits as they are approved for release. The project advances in stages, and we state plainly what is proven, what is not yet proven, and what we still do not know.

body: The name Jalaranu combines “jala”, understood as water in the naming of this brand, and “ranu”, lake. Its visual identity draws inspiration from Javanese heritage.
A guardian goddess supports a datacenter beneath flowing water. The symbol expresses a responsibility to safeguard knowledge and the infrastructure that supports it.
That meaning carries into the way the project is developed: clear questions, focused testing, and honest communication about findings and limitations.

items.title: Responsibility across the facility's life
items.body: Planning covers installation, operation, recovery, and end of life.

items.title: Collaboration with clear roles
items.body: Contributions, interfaces, and responsibilities are agreed from the outset.

items.title: Proportionate openness
items.body: Public information explains the project rationale; detailed discussion follows need and access authority.

team.body: Jalaranu is built by dedicated people who believe Indonesian infrastructure should be built on measured evidence, not assumptions: engineers, security practitioners, and strategists who publish the project's questions and methods, and share findings that are approved for release. The work is organised across three partners with complementary roles: COCONUT Computer Club leads the engineering, PERKAMINDO is responsible for information security, and PT Lontar Riset Indonesia for strategy and business. Collaboration remains open to other parties who share the project's standards.

paper.body: The engineering reasoning, threat model, thermal screening, and cost comparison behind this project are documented in an open paper. Read it directly or save a copy.
